title: Measurement and Geometry - Lesson 10 Practice: Volume Design Task
description: Practice comparing cylinder and pyramid containers using volume, capacity conversion, and design reasoning.

questions.question: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 14 cm. Using pi = 3.14, what is its volume?
A square pyramid has base side length 9 cm and vertical height 12 cm. What is its volume?
A container has volume 875 cm^3. How many milliliters can it hold? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Since 1 cm^3 = 1 mL, 875 cm^3 equals 875 mL.

questions.question: A design must hold at least 500 mL. A cylinder holds 565 cm^3 and a pyramid holds 480 cm^3. Which design meets the need?
questions.explanation: 565 cm^3 = 565 mL, which is at least 500 mL. 480 cm^3 = 480 mL, which is less than 500 mL.

questions.question: A pyramid with the same base area and height as a prism has one-third of the prism's volume.
questions.explanation: The pyramid formula is V = (1/3)Bh, so it has one-third the volume of a prism with the same base area B and height h.

questions.question: A rectangular pyramid has length 10 cm, width 6 cm, and height 9 cm. Find its volume in cm^3. Enter just the number.
A container has capacity 1.35 L. What is this capacity in milliliters?
A snack booth needs at least 1 L of capacity. Design A holds 980 mL. Design B holds 1,080 cm^3. Which design should be chosen, and why?
questions.correctAnswer: Design B should be chosen because 1080 cm^3 equals 1080 mL, or 1.08 L. Design A holds only 980 mL, which is less than 1 L.
questions.explanation: A complete answer converts 1080 cm^3 to 1080 mL, compares both designs to 1000 mL, and chooses the one that meets the need.
